:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="49%"}

### Preprocessing

::: {.workflow-step}
**Leakage control**

Excluded identifiers and rating-derived predictors.
:::

::: {.workflow-step}
**Data handling**

Handled unknown, novel and rare categorical levels; median-imputed numeric missingness.
:::

::: {.workflow-step}
**Transformation**

Applied $\log(x+1)$ to provider service count.
:::

::: {.workflow-step}
**Model-specific recipes**

Scaled recipe: normalization, dummy encoding and NZV removal.

Tree recipe: dummy encoding and NZV removal without normalization.
:::

:::

::: {.column width="49%"}

### Grouped evaluation

::: {.evaluation-step}
**80/20 grouped split**

Services from the same provider remained in one partition.
:::

::: {.evaluation-step}
**Five-fold grouped cross-validation**

No provider crossed the analysis and validation sets; all models used the same folds.
:::

::: {.evaluation-step}
**Evaluation metrics**

Primary: **Macro-F1**

Secondary: accuracy and class-specific recall.
:::

::: {.evaluation-step}
**Final evaluation**

The held-out test set was reserved until model selection.
:::

:::

::::

::: {.fold-rule}
**Fold-wise rule:** preprocessing parameters were estimated from training data only.
:::

::: {.notes}
We used a shared preprocessing and evaluation workflow for all five models. Identifiers and rating-derived variables were excluded, while missing values, categorical levels and model-specific scaling were handled through recipes. Because one provider may operate several services, we performed both the 80/20 split and five-fold cross-validation at provider level. Macro-F1 was the primary metric because the rating tiers were strongly imbalanced, and the held-out test set was reserved for final evaluation.
:::
